text:
sam: quick question — proposal for soft-pin handshake semantics. want to validate before i write an rfc.

mira: go for it, high level first pls. what problem are we solving?

sam: tenants sometimes hold soft-pins for short canary runs. current TTL-only approach causes a race when ops wants to force-roll back a model in a region. TTLs expire later and client routing keeps hitting the pinned variant.

kevin: yep seconded. we hit that when a canary hung and we needed immediate fallback. ops had to manually reconcile caches. not great.

jordan: what's the proposed signal? eviction token? lease revocation?

sam: idea: introduce a small lease token + revocation counter in rollout metadata. semantics: soft-pin = {variant, lease_id, lease_expiry, rev_counter}. clients accept pin if lease_id matches last seen and rev_counter == stored. control plane can increment rev_counter to force immediate invalidation.

mira: sounds promising. how do we keep it safe across regions and network partitions?

sam: two parts: 1) leases are short (e.g., 30s–5m) for soft-pins; 2) rev_counter is monotonic per rollout id and replicated via strong write to config store. clients poll for rev_counter on every pull or via push notifications.

kevin: polling every pull is heavy for high-qps clients. can we piggyback rev_counter on existing health/telemetry hooks?

jordan: or expose it on prefix cache-invalidation pubsub channel so runtime only subscribes once.

sam: agreed — push-based invalidation where available, fallback to lightweight conditional polling (if last_poll+poll_jitter > lease_expiry/2 then pull).

mira: how about backward compat? older clients that don't understand rev_counter should default to TTL-only (graceful). but control plane should mark rollouts with a compatibility-bit to avoid using rev_counter-only guarantees for mixed fleets.

kevin: we also need to reason about pinning + quantized variants. if a tenant pins to q4_0 profile, fallback must choose closest compatible variant. will rev_counter be per-variant or per-rollout?

sam: per-rollout id (rollout_id) with metadata listing compatible variants. rev_counter increments for the whole rollout. a forced rollback will set next active variant index and rev_counter++. clients then reconcile to the new active variant set.

jordan: include small example metadata snippet?

sam: sure — example payload:

```json
{
  "rollout_id": "rlt-2026-09-21-42",
  "active_variant": "v2-quant-q4",
  "compatible_variants": ["v2-quant-q4","v2-raw-fp16","v1-compat-q8"],
  "lease_id": "lease-9a8b",
  "lease_expiry": "2026-09-21T18:03:00Z",
  "rev_counter": 7,
  "pin_type": "soft",
  "scope": "tenant:acme-corp",
  "origin": "canary-controller"
}
```

mira: couple nitpicks: 1) use unix epoch for lease_expiry to simplify comparisons in runtime; 2) pin_type enum should include 'hard' and 'soft' and maybe 'sticky' for special cases.

sam: good call. will change expiry. also plan to add "force_evict" boolean that's only set by ops during emergencies — increments rev_counter and sets active_variant to fallback.

kevin: how do we prevent rev_counter churn from breaking telemetry and rollout analytics? every rev_counter change will be an event — we should emit structured events with reason + operator id. ops-bot: can you create a short audit event spec?

ops-bot: created ticket INF-4123: "rollout rev_counter audit events". schema: {rollout_id, prev_rev, new_rev, reason, actor, timestamp}. link: https://tickets.redwood.ai/INF-4123

jordan: we also need to defend against spurious increments (accidental operator click). maybe a two-phase forced-evict: operator marks reason + dry-run flag, system validates safety checks (traffic-shift ban windows) and then allows final apply which increments rev_counter. UI should require confirmation for immediate evictions.

mira: reaction: :thumbsup: to two-phase apply. also add a cooldown period where rev_counter increments are rate-limited per rollout to avoid oscillation.

kevin: rollout resolution on the runtime side: when rev_counter changes, runtime should drop prefix caches and KV entries for that rollout id, and optionally flush batching state for pinned requests. This is disruptive but required for safety. we should document the expected cost and provide a grace toggle for low-latency-critical tenants.

sam: yes. we'll add a tenant-level flag allow_radical_invalidation = true/false. default false for enterprise.

mira: operationally, how do we test? propose a canary harness: simulate cross-region partition, set rev_counter remotely, verify runtimes subscribe and invalidate within 2x lease_expiry. add automated chaos tests in CI.

jordan: also add metrics: time_to_invalidation, number_of_missed_polls, fallback_rate_after_rev. tie alerts to thresholds.

sam: next steps: i'll draft a short rfc with these parts: 1) metadata schema change (lease_id, rev_counter, force_evict, compatible_variants, expiry as epoch), 2) runtime semantics (push-first, poll-fallback, cache eviction behavior), 3) control plane ops flow (two-phase eviction, audit events, rate limits), 4) migration plan for older clients.

mira: sounds good. aim for a succinct design doc + sequence diagrams. pls ping infra for strong-write path for rev_counter.

kevin: tagging infra: @kevin for the replication/consistency question — do we need linearizable writes for rev_counter?

kevin: my take: rev_counter must be strongly ordered per-rollout id. if we use leader-writes in the control plane and versioned updates in the store, that's enough. global linearizability across regions is ideal but probably overkill; a regional leader plus cross-region anti-entropy should work if lease expiries are conservative.

jordan: ok, i'm happy to help draft the sequence diagrams. sam, assign me for the runtime invalidation section.

sam: thanks all — i'll create the rfc draft tomorrow and link it here. :wave:
